intro: The United Arab Emirates is a union of seven emirates that went from pearl diving and fishing villages to gleaming cities in about fifty years.

chapters.title: Ancient trade
text: People have lived here for over 100,000 years. In the Bronze Age, the land called Magan traded copper with Mesopotamia; tombs at Hili and Umm an-Nar date from that time.
Islam arrived in the 600s. Coastal towns lived from fishing, trade and pearl diving, while Bedouin herded camels inland and farmers grew dates in oases like Al Ain and Liwa.

chapters.title: The Trucial States
text: In the 1800s Britain signed truces with the local sheikhs to stop attacks on shipping, and the area became known as the Trucial States. Britain controlled their foreign affairs.
The pearl trade collapsed in the 1930s when Japan invented cultured pearls, bringing hard times.

chapters.title: Oil and union
text: Oil was found in Abu Dhabi in 1958 and exports began in 1962. When Britain left in 1971, six emirates joined together on 2 December under Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan; Ras Al Khaimah joined in 1972.
Oil money built roads, schools and hospitals. Dubai turned itself into a trading, tourism and finance hub, and in 2020 the UAE sent a probe to Mars.

highlight.title: Fast change
highlight.text: In 1960 Dubai had no paved roads; today it has the world's tallest building.

timeline.title: Union
timeline.text: The UAE is formed on 2 December.
